steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Beat softened butter and sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in vanilla; add flour gradually, mixing until a smooth dough forms.

Fill cookie press with dough and form cookies onto two ungreased cookie sheets, spacing them about 1 ½ inches apart. Bake in the preheated oven until the edges of the cookies are just starting to turn golden brown, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove the cookie sheets from the oven, and set them on a wire cooling rack for a few minutes. Then transfer the shortbread cookies to the rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Shortbread Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These classic shortbread cookies are buttery, tender, and melt in your mouth—made with just 4 ingredients and perfect for holiday cookie trays.

video.description: Skip the tin cookies and make your own with this simple 4-ingredient recipe! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make easy shortbread cookies for the holiday season. These melt-in-your-mouth cookies are made by combining butter, sugar, vanilla, and flour into a smooth dough. After rolling out and shaping the cookie dough into individual cookies, bake them in the oven for around 10 minutes. They’re soft, tender, and a delicious festive treat that the whole family will enjoy.

review.reviewBody: After making the dough instead of using a cookie press or dropping by balls, I rolled the dough into four logs, wrapped the logs in waxed paper, placed in the fridge to harden, and then sliced in about 1/2" slices. Perfect and delicious. Sometimes I make the dough up to 3 days ahead of time then slice and bake when I need them. After baked I sprinkle with powder sugar. Makes a beauiful presentation.

Wonderful shortbread cookie! These were so easy to make and yet turned out fabulous. It's great when such simple ingredients come together to create something so delicious! I followed the recipe exactly and let the dough chill in the fridge for a half hour before rolling it out and using cookie cutters vs. a cookie press. I baked the cookies on parchment paper and they were perfectly done in ten minutes. These have a wonderful butter flavor and are great for decorating. When I was all done I placed them in clear cellophane bags tied with ribbon - too cute!

I read the reviews that mentioned the dough was too dry or crumbly. Keep in mind that when our old Scottish grannies were making these cookies for their families, they DID NOT have a $300 fancy-pants mixer. They had a sturdy spoon and strong arms. As you add the flour and it's crumbly, dump it all out onto a parchment paper on your bread board. Wash your hands well and then grab those crumbles and begin to press them into a ball. Keep gently turning and pressing those crumbles and you'll suddenly see something magical happen. The warmth from your skin will soften the butter and the next thing you know you have a smooth creamy dough. You can lay another piece of parchment over your dough ball and roll it smooth and flat to your desired thickness. This isn't rocket science. The old grannies knew more than we give them credit for. Enjoy.

I’m curious as to where this recipe was found. This is the exact recipe my mother had made since the 1950s. She referred to them as butter cookies. She used the Mirror cookie press and red and green food coloring at Christmas time. Also, her recipe included 1/4 tsp of mace. Because the recipe was in her handwritten cookbook, I have no idea where it originated. I’d appreciate it if anyone has any history on this recipe. Thanks.

I just made these to take to a social gathering and of course I had to try them first and wow, so good! I followed the recipe exactly, except I didn't have a cookie press or cookie cutters, so I chilled the dough for 30 minutes and rolled in to walnut size balls, rolled them in powdered sugar and suggested by another reviewer, and then pressed down on them slightly with the bottom of a teacup. After they were cooled, I melted some milk chocolate chips, put in a ziploc bag, cut the tip, and drizzled it over the cookies. They look great, and taste even better. Can't wait to see how my friends enjoy them!

Delicious recipe. I added 2tbs of fresh chopped lemon balm to the batter. After the cookies were baked I dipped half of each cookie in white chocolate and topped with chopped pistachios and dried rose petals. Fantastic!

Just made them and they are so good! I used land o lakes spreadable butter and it was so much easier as I didn’t have to wait for it to soften yet it still had same buttery taste and consistency. I did roll batter into two rolls using Saran Wrap and put in fridge for an hour to harden then sliced them. I baked for 15 minutes and then dipped in chocolate ganache. These are my new go to cookies!

I use 1 cup less flour and 1/2 cup of cornstarch mixed into butter sugar mix. Roll into balls smaller than golf balls and use thumb to flatten to 1/2 inch thick. Put half a maraschino cherry (red) on each and bake for 20 to 25 min at 325 F . Should make about 45 cookies

We have made them twice already and they were eaten quickly by 3 adults! We don’t have a cookie press so we gently rolled the cookie dough and cut with cookie cutter. We will definitely make them again. Sooooo delicious.

I followed the recipe exactly and the cookies turned out spectacular. The only thing, since I don't own a cookie press, I just rolled the dough into a walnut sized balls rolled in a bit of sugar and pressed them lightly with the bottom of a glass. Perfect, uniform shaped cookies. Overall amazing.

This recipe turned out to be just what I hoped for! I followed the recipe as stated and rolled the dough into balls and slightly flattened them before setting on ungreased cookie sheets. I halved the recipe and it made a little over 2 dozen for me. I experimented and melted chocolate chips and dipped the cooled cookies into the chocolate, set in freezer half an hour and that was tasty! Honestly, I enjoyed the cookie alone with no chocolate. I highly recommend this recipe.

I made exactly the recipe, except that I used 1 cup whole wheat + 3 cups white/unbleached flour. I used a small drinking glass to cut the cookies and it worked pretty well. The one problem is that someone in my household lost one of the beaters from our KitchenAid handheld mixer, so I had to make do with a single beater blade and it was a bit sloppy and unstable, though it worked okay I guess. (I've ordered a replacement set from Amazon.) Anyway, the cookies came out absolutely delicious. I will be making this again!
I cut the recipe in half. Easy quick cookie to make and tasted great. I rolled each cookie into balls then flatten them a little bit with a fork.
I make these quite often, very simple and delish. I make half a batch and it makes about 24 cookies, yum!
Amazing, just amazing

I add chocolate chips (I prefer Ghirardelli milk chocolate chips, I think the flavors work best together) and form them into balls and flatten by hand. Definitely makes way more than 2 dozen though. I'm well known amongst my friends for these and everyone loves them! I have also made them vegan and gluten free, with unsalted vegan butter and Trader Joe's gluten free flour. A slightly different flavor and texture, but still delicious!
Needed a little bit more sugar, anout 1/4 of a cup more sugar gor a delightful little cookies for any occasion.
I used half salted butter and half Irish butter which has more fat, I think next time i’m using all Irish butter. I’ll let you know!
Ten minutes wasn't long enough but 11 minutes was too long. Way too much butter - they come out greasy. Too much flour; ¾ flour and ¼ cornstarch would shorten these up. Overall, it's a fail.

I went off the map, using organic whole wheat spelt flour, 1/2 vegan margarine & 1/2 coconut oil, and added peppermint extract to the mix. I don’t have a mixer, so creamed the butter and sugar manually. I also hand-pressed them on parchment paper on a cookie sheet…except I have a pizza stone not a cookie sheet…and topped them with crushed peppermint sticks. They were freakin’ delicious even though I was really cavalier with the recipe.
